2025 (arXiv v1 2025; v6 dated 22 May 2026)
Preprint — arXiv:2512.18470v6 [cs.SE]; no venue stated (appendix mentions anonymous review)

Industry and academia: FPT Software AI Center, Ha Noi, Viet Nam (Le, Pham, Phan); School of Computing and Information Systems, University of Melbourne (Nguyen Manh); Center of AI Research, VinUniversity, Ha Noi (Bui, project lead)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — SWE-EVO benchmark (48 release-sized software-evolution tasks from 7 Python projects, specified by release notes, validated by FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests) and a new soft metric, Fix Rate; evaluation of 18 models with OpenHands and SWE-agent

Coding-agent scaffolds compared: OpenHands (CodeActAgent, max 100 iterations) and SWE-agent (max 100 LLM calls); no versions. 18 models: gpt-5.4, gpt-5.2, gpt-5-08-07, gpt-5-mini-08-07, gpt-5-nano-08-07, o3-2025-04-16, gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, gpt-4o-2024-11-20, gpt-oss-120b, deepseek-v3p2, deepseek-v3p1, deepseek-r1-0528, glm-5, glm-4p7, glm-4p5, qwen3-coder-480b-a35b, kimi-k2p5, kimi-k2-instruct; medium reasoning effort for reasoning models. No SDD approach

Benchmark input (not an approach): release-note-centred 'Software Requirement Specification' = official release-note delta between two tagged versions, by default augmented with the bodies of linked PRs/issues appended verbatim; plus the full codebase at the start version. Output: a multi-file model patch

No prescribed flow: agent receives release note (+ PR/issue context) and start-version codebase, works within its scaffold (internet blocked) and produces a patch, evaluated on FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests. Benchmark construction: (I) repository selection from SWE-bench and SWE-gym seed pool; (II) candidates whose base commit is a release tag, problem statement = release-note delta; (III) execution-based filtering (at least one FAIL_TO_PASS test, no install/runtime errors); manual verification down to 48 instances
None during agent runs. Human verification only in benchmark construction (alignment of release note, PR/issue context, gold patch and tests)
Full agent run from release-note specification to patch (the specification is the benchmark input, not an SDD workflow)
Not classifiable (benchmark of coding agents; authors call release notes 'Software Requirement Specifications' but no SDD approach)
Existing code base: evolve a mature open-source Python project from one release to the next

48 instances from 7 repositories (dvc 26, dask 8, requests 4, pydantic 3, modin 3, conan 2, scikit-learn 2). Per instance (mean/max): spec 2,390.5/22,344 words; codebase 363/1,046 non-test files and 78K/272K non-test lines; gold patch 610.5/4,113 lines, 20.9/105 files, 51.0/379 functions edited; 81.4/2,774 FAIL_TO_PASS and 874.0/8,552 total tests; median 6 linked PRs
Popular PyPI Python libraries (data versioning, parallel computing, HTTP, data validation, dataframes, package management, machine learning)
N/A (no human participants)

Resolved Rate (%) (instance resolved when all FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests pass); Patch Apply Rate (%); Fix Rate (%) (new soft metric: fraction of FAIL_TO_PASS tests fixed, 0 if any PASS_TO_PASS test fails); diagnostic relaxed FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS rates
None (authors state Fix Rate does not measure code quality, maintainability or patch minimality)
None

Failure-mode distribution of unresolved SWE-agent trajectories (Syntax Error, Incorrect Implementation, Instruction Following, Tool-Use, Stuck in Loop, Gave Up Prematurely, Other); empirical difficulty groups and PRs per instance; turns by difficulty group; per-repository Resolved and Fix rates

Automatic: patch applied and test suites run in instance-level Docker images (pytest -rA, log parser), following SWE-bench harness; 95% Wilson confidence intervals for representative rates. Failure modes labelled automatically by an LLM judge (gpt-5-mini), one primary label per trajectory; human agreement not validated

fields.v: Tasks: 48 SWE-EVO instances. Configurations: 18 models x 2 scaffolds (OpenHands CodeActAgent max 100 iterations; SWE-agent max 100 LLM calls); two input settings (release note only; release note + PR/issue context, default). Baseline: none; models' SWE-bench Verified scores (from swebench.com) used as reference. Held constant: instances, Docker environments, iteration budget per scaffold, medium reasoning effort, internet blocked. Acceptance tests: FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests from the upstream release. Repetitions: not stated (single run implied). Human intervention: none stated

Best: gpt-5.4 25% on both scaffolds by Resolved Rate in the abstract, though glm-4p7 (39.58%) and glm-5 (37.50%) score higher with SWE-agent in Table 2. gpt-5.2 drops from 72.80% on SWE-bench Verified to 22.92% on SWE-EVO. Larger models generally beat smaller variants; glm-5/glm-4p7 show strong scaffold sensitivity (OpenHands 8.33/4.17 vs SWE-agent 37.50/39.58). Adding PR/issue context generally improves resolved rates modestly, ranking preserved. Fix Rate separates models tied on Resolved Rate (gpt-4.1 4.65% vs gpt-oss-120b 2.08%). Failure analysis: gpt-5 failures >60% Instruction Following; smaller/older models more tool-use, syntax, looping. No significance tests; Wilson 95% CIs e.g. [14.9, 38.8] for 25.00%

Distinguished large gaps between models and showed scaffold sensitivity; authors state that with 48 instances one instance = 2.08 points, close leaderboard gaps should not be over-interpreted (wide Wilson CIs). Fix Rate added to separate ties. Repeatability not assessed. Limitations stated: Python only, release-note-centred specs, 48 instances with imbalance toward dvc (26/48) limiting statistical power, Fix Rate weights tests equally and ignores code quality; LLM-judge failure labels not validated against humans

Python library projects only (multilingual and application evolution future work); specifications are release-note-centred, not covering security advisories, dependency updates or design-document-driven refactors; 48 instances, imbalanced toward dvc, limited statistical power; Fix Rate weights tests equally and does not measure code quality, maintainability or patch minimality; sequential PR-by-PR variant future work; human validation of failure-mode judge future work. Gap: agents struggle with sustained multi-file reasoning and release-level evolution

Inconsistencies: abstract/conclusion say best model gpt-5.4 reaches 25%, but Table 2/6 give glm-4p7 39.58% and glm-5 37.50% with SWE-agent (abstract 'best model' holds only for OpenHands or for average); o3 SWE-agent Resolved 6.25 in Tables 2 and 4 vs 4.17 in Table 6; deepseek-v3p2 SWE-agent 23.40% is not a multiple of 1/48 (2.08 points); gpt-5.2 SWE-bench Verified 'around 75%' (p. 2) vs 72.80% (Table 2). Values taken from Table 6 (and Table 2 for Apply). Data: GitHub URL github.com/SWE-EVO/SWE-EVO; appendix K says metadata, scripts, Docker config, harness, generated patches and results 'will' be released. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python
